chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, there is nothing wherein there is either a constriction or an extension from what God has commanded or forbidden, except that therein, for God Mighty and Majestic, is a trial and an ordainment.

key_terms.ابْتِلَاءٌ: Trial, tribulation, divine testing — the purpose of every command is to examine the believer
key_terms.بَسْطٌ: Extension, expansion — referring to permissive rulings that allow latitude and ease
key_terms.قَبْضٌ: Constriction, restriction — referring to prohibitions and obligations that restrain the believer's actions
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: Divine ordainment, decree — God's sovereign will expressed through His commands and prohibitions

ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind divine commands and prohibitions in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that every divine command and prohibition carries within it both a divine trial (ibtila') and a divine decree (qada'). Whether the ruling involves restriction (qabdh) or permission (bast), the underlying purpose is always twofold: to test the believer's compliance and to fulfill God's overarching will. This hadith frames the entire corpus of religious law as simultaneously a test of faith and an expression of divine wisdom.
